verdict_text:
YES

The script drops blocks 2, 6, 10, 14, renumbers the survivors in original order via an injective old-to-new map (0,1,3,4,5,7,8,9,11,12,13,15 to 0..11), passes the two non-block tensors through untouched, and writes a single `out/T1/model.safetensors`. The check that the surviving layer index set equals exactly {0..11} covers both "no blocks 12-15 remain" and "exactly 12 blocks remain", and the 86-tensor count is asserted; both assertions run before the output is written, so failure leaves no output. The only observations are that it depends on a sandbox helper `_ckpt.load_checkpoint` for reading the sharded input, and the checks use `assert`, which would be skipped under `python -O`; neither violates a specification clause.
